subject.title: Feature: Claude usage source via minimal inference call reading anthropic-ratelimit-unified-* headers (multi-account with setup-tokens / user:inference)

question: Should CodexBar support an opt-in setup-token inference-polling source for Claude unified usage, despite relying on undocumented headers and consuming a small amount of plan quota on each refresh?
rationale: The owner has validated feasibility but has not selected the lasting credential, polling, labeling, and fallback contract; those choices affect user expectations and provider behavior beyond a mechanical parser fix.

options.title: Approve a scoped opt-in source
options.body: Add a clearly labeled setup-token source that polls only on user-enabled refresh intervals, preserves OAuth/web defaults, and uses captured-header fixtures plus model fallbacks.

options.title: Defer to generic multi-account work
options.body: Resolve generic provider-instance/account semantics first, then add this Claude-specific source within that approved model.

options.title: Decline inference polling
options.body: Keep current usage sources and avoid making real inference calls solely to obtain usage metadata from undocumented headers.

recommendation.title: Approve a scoped opt-in source
recommendation.body: Add a clearly labeled setup-token source that polls only on user-enabled refresh intervals, preserves OAuth/web defaults, and uses captured-header fixtures plus model fallbacks.

likelyOwner.reason: The owner authored the current feasibility guidance and is best positioned to choose the supported Claude usage-source contract.
